item.title: In Britain, we equate blackness with the working class. It’s time for a rethink
item.summary: In my new book, I narrate the existence, behaviours and sensibilities of the black British middle class, a social group largely ignored, until now Don’t already get The Long Wave in your inbox? Sign up here While narrating the audio version of my new book, The Good, the Black and the Boujee , came a revelatory reminder of why many black Britons see middle class status as a “white people ting”. After a recording session, I headed upstairs to see if I could find any friendly faces from my publisher before heading out into the sweltering heatwave for my cycle home. To my disappointment, I found a near-empty office floor, and left minutes later. Donning my helmet, I joined the middle class commuters who regularly left the office in cycling gear. As I approached the exit, something peculiar happened: I was met with a friendly expression of relief from the reception staff. The building had received a concerned report about a potential intruder on the top floor, they told me. The intruder was believed to be a rogue courier who had somehow passed the loading bay and made it into the editorial offices. It took me a moment to realise – the intruding courier was … me.
